A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JuStRank study. All 31 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–G, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments generating approximately 1.5 million judgment scores from 48 judge realizations, with ranking results and analyses of decisiveness and bias.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their numerical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The four judge realizations, score mappings, aggregation methods, and decisiveness and bias computations are unchanged. Appendix G retains identical prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Arena Hard v0.1 responses, Chatbot Arena English Hard Prompts reference data, and RewardBench comparisons. Releasing existing judgment scores does not add evaluated data or tasks.

E2.justification: The same eight reward models and ten LLMs participate in the comparisons. Llama-3-70B-Instruct is added to the prose list in Section 4.2.2 but already appears in v1's Table 2. Favi-Score is newly discussed, not evaluated.

E3.justification: Both retain 500 instructions, 63 target systems, 59 systems overlapping with the gold data, and 968 system pairs. Metrics, aggregation procedures, data filtering, and evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The realization comparisons, score-distribution analyses, beta fits, system-specific biases, and self-bias analyses are retained without substantive revision. No new ablation or robustness experiment is reported.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains its 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. Appendix D retains the ANOVA and Tukey HSD analyses, while Table 3 retains one-sided paired t-tests with Bonferroni correction. Run and seed reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the result plots retain the same numerical and qualitative findings. For example, Table 2 reports Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct/Likert/Win-Rate at tau 0.827 and URM/Mean at 0.823 in both versions.

T1.justification: The formal task formulation, bias definitions, aggregation formulas, pairwise metrics, and beta-fitting objective are unchanged. The new Favi-Score comparison explains positioning without revising the mathematics.

C1.justification: v2 adds a fourth introductory contribution: releasing 1.5 million judgment scores, also mentioned in the Discussion. The abstract and central claims about system ranking, decisiveness, and bias retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: A new Section 6.2 footnote explains that the bias measure captures practical effects on system preference, contrasting it with Favi-Score's separation from overall accuracy. The Limitations section additionally acknowledges dependence on the API and inference implementation.

D1.justification: v1 documents prompts and source data but provides no access link for its generated judgments. v2 announces and links the 1.5-million-score JuStRank dataset in Introduction footnote 1, substantially extending reproducibility and reuse information. It also corrects the prose model roster to include the already-evaluated Llama-3-70B-Instruct.

R1.justification: v2 adds Panickssery et al. on self-favoring evaluators and two von Däniken et al. works on system dependence and Favi-Score. These provide additional context and a specific distinction between bias measures without substantially changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: There are localized wording edits in the introduction, related work, discussion, and conclusion, plus a corrected model list and movement of the prompt-reference footnote into the body. The main section order and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures and tables retain their content and structure. Added text and footnotes cause limited layout reflow, including Figure 3 moving downward and Appendix A beginning on page 13 rather than sharing page 12 with references.

improvement.justification: v2 improves documented access to the existing judgment data, corrects the model roster, and clarifies the bias measure and implementation sensitivity. These support reuse and interpretation. The PDFs show no new validation or substantive correction to the empirical conclusions, so the overall quality improvement is limited despite the substantial data-access addition.
